conclusion: A separately implemented cached noncoherent dma-buf exporter is supported by standard kernel APIs on this configured arm64 direct-DMA platform, but the current WC exporter and WC-only userspace contract cannot be made correct by changing the mmap cache attribute alone. Cached access requires a matched allocation/mapping/free API, ownership transitions and real DMA synchronization for every CPU/device path.
current_contract: ve_heap_allocate uses dma_alloc_wc; ve_buffer_mmap uses dma_mmap_wc; release uses dma_free_wc. All aliases must stay compatible with that allocation until a separate implementation exists.

Exporter begin/end_cpu_access and legacy cache ioctl only issue barriers. The matching MemAdapter explicitly assumes no WB alias and ion_alloc_flush_cache only executes dmb osh after range validation. These barriers cannot clean or invalidate cached CPU lines.
Only same-device private dma-bufs are accepted, the driver rejects an IOMMU-mapped device and uses a32-bit mask. Imported mappings stay quarantined until reboot.
standard_api_path: dma_alloc_noncoherent(dev,size,&dma,dir,GFP_KERNEL) is an inline dma_alloc_pages/page_address wrapper; using dma_alloc_pages directly retains the struct page needed by dma_mmap_pages.
dma_mmap_pages(dev,vma,size,page) maps those allocated pages using normal VMA protection and bounds; this kernel has no dma_mmap_noncoherent API. Do not remap a live dma_alloc_wc allocation as WB.
The matching free API is dma_free_pages or dma_free_noncoherent with the same device,size,handle,direction. Keep the existing quarantine policy for any buffer whose DMA address was disclosed.

Keep the same-device attachment restriction and represent the already allocated/mapped pages and DMA handle in the scatterlist. Do not add a second streaming mapping or silently accept a bounce/IOMMU/foreign-buffer path. Retain all-pages contiguity,identity and32-bit-end checks.

Use dma_sync_single_for_cpu before CPU access after confirmed device completion and dma_sync_single_for_device after CPU writes and before the next device access. Allocation/map/free/sync directions must be consistent; a BIDIRECTIONAL allocation is a conservative candidate for buffers whose roles change, not permission to overlap CPU/device writes.

For arm64 arch_sync_dma_for_device cleans to PoC; arch_sync_dma_for_cpu invalidates to PoC except DMA_TO_DEVICE. The generic helpers dispatch the platform behavior; a hand-written barrier or arbitrary user-VA flush does not substitute.
configuration_readback_scope: Build config only, not a fresh board runtime check. CONFIG_IOMMU_SUPPORT=n; DMA_NEED_SYNC, DMA_NONCOHERENT_MMAP, DMA_DIRECT_REMAP, DMA_CMA, CMA=y; CMA256MiB. DT has no dma-coherent or iommus property for VE. Runtime device/DT/mapping conditions would need independent confirmation for a new candidate.
ownership_and_userspace_gaps: dma-buf START/END is a cache-access bracket, not a hardware stop primitive. This driver does not publish VE completion fences in dma_resv; callers must prove explicit completion and no overlapping device writes before beginning CPU access.

The GStreamer DmaBuf allocator source has DMA_BUF_IOCTL_SYNC START/END around GstMemory mapping. This is useful for the decoded frame read bracket but does not cover the permanently mapped vendor input/scratch/reference-buffer aliases. Confirm the installed GStreamer binary actually enables HAVE_LINUX_DMA_BUF_H.

The reviewed GstDmaBuf map/unmap implementation logs synchronization ioctl failures as warnings and continues; a cached path must propagate failures or otherwise fail closed before using possibly stale bytes.

MemAdapter CdcIonMmap permanently maps read/write memory; ion_alloc_flush_cache is currently WC-only and carries no explicit read/write ownership state. All vendor input writes, parameter/scratch initialization, decoded output reads and buffer returns must be audited and paired with the appropriate sync transitions.

A generic FlushCache callback cannot blindly clean/invalidate while VE owns the buffer. A directionless combined flush can overwrite device output or expose stale data if called at the wrong ownership point.

Page-size allocations isolate boundary cache lines from unrelated objects, but simultaneous alias users/threads and multiple START/END brackets still need a defined ownership/nesting policy. Whole-buffer synchronization is safer to reason about first; any range optimization needs cache-line boundary proof.
not_solved: No IOMMU isolation or proof of AXI/DMA drain is added.
No safe imported-buffer reuse or quarantine release is added.
No60fps or performance gain follows from API feasibility; compare end-to-end counters, copy costs and exact pixels/PTS after any independently reviewed implementation.
Current v27/v28 kernels and WC library packages remain unchanged by this review.
